A1.justification: Both complete 36-page PDFs describe the same AFIP research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison, including matching content relocated between pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original CHAIR and POPE evaluations, attention diagnostics, component and layer ablations, parameter studies, and qualitative model outputs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and Appendix D, including benchmark comparisons and ablation studies.

M1.justification: AFIP retains the same top-k head correction, historical attention enhancement, dynamic gating, and layer-selection procedure. Equations (5)-(12) and Algorithm 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate COCO-based image descriptions using CHAIR and object-existence questions using POPE's random, popular, and adversarial settings. The appendix examples introduce no changed task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment: Table 1 includes Greedy, Beam, OPERA, VCD, MemVR, and HGAI; Tables 2-3 retain the same set without OPERA. Appendix comparison groups also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain unchanged, including 500 sampled MSCOCO 2014 validation images, beam size 5, the model configurations, 512-token main evaluations, and the 64/128/256-token length study. Appendix C retains the same prompts and metrics.

E4.justification: The attention diagnostics, generation-length analysis, component ablations, layer-selection study, parameter sweeps, and qualitative case studies are retained. Appendix D contains no added or removed analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 2,000 bootstrap resampling trials, significance and correlation testing, and standard-deviation shading. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding entries in Tables 1-5 and the plotted and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains AFIP's LLaVA-1.5-7B scores of CS=16.8, CI=4.4, and precision=91.3. Relocated figures do not introduce new results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 5.1-5.2, assumptions, and derivations are unchanged. Appendices A-B preserve the same complete proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about spatial attention inconsistency, temporal fading, generalization, and AFIP's training-free hallucination mitigation. The no-additional-inference-overhead claim is also retained.

C2.justification: Explanations of spatial and temporal mechanisms, the rationale for gating and avoiding early-layer intervention, and interpretations of comparative results remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-availability statement and GitHub repository address to the abstract, absent from v1. Other implementation and experimental details are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The introduction and bibliography remove LLaVA-Med, Yang et al.'s medical multi-image VLM paper, and Huang et al.'s hallucination survey, while adding three Li et al. papers on multi-view/multi-label learning. Section 2 and the core novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: the code statement, introductory citations, punctuation, and addition of Tingjin Luo as a corresponding author. The substantive prose and section sequence are retained without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 3 to 4, Figure 4 from page 5 to 6, and text reflow moves the conclusion to page 10. Tables retain their structure. Appendix qualitative figures show small rendering differences while preserving the same examples and annotations.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer improves discoverability, but replacing directly relevant medical-MLLM references with multi-view/multi-label papers makes support for the introductory context less clear. Methods, evidence, and proofs remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the linked code's reproducibility value, so these mixed documentation changes do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
